source:
Make a simple 3D endless runner. Keep it simple - do NOT do prompt
enhancement or a big requirements write-up, and don't expand the scope. I
just want one small, polished, ~5-minute playable game, nothing more.

- Fully 3D (render a real WebGL scene). Works on mobile, touch and mouse,
 in both portrait and landscape.
- Third-person camera behind and slightly above the runner, looking down
 the track.
- The runner auto-runs forward; tap/swipe left-right to switch lanes,
 tap/swipe up to jump. Dodge obstacles and grab coins. Speed increases
 slowly over time.
- Crashing into an obstacle ends the run - show the run distance and coins
 with a Retry button.
- Save the player's best distance on the server and show it in the HUD.

That's the whole game. No shops, no extra modes, no upgrade systems - just
the core run loop, made to feel good.

image_prompt.text: Modular track segments emitted ahead of the runner, exit pivot matching the next origin pivot so the lane strip never drifts over a long run
Occasional lane-crossing obstacles timed against the runner's current speed
Low barriers across the lanes for the runner to hurdle on a swipe up
Contact with an obstacle ends the run outright - the obstacles are the only failure state

layout_placement.text: Coin trails laid along the lanes, positioned to pull the runner across into riskier lines

notes: Obstacle spacing must stay elastic against the slowly rising speed, since the prompt has speed increase over time and a single obstacle contact ends the run.
The prompt is explicit that scope must not be expanded; the preset's moving-obstacle option is retained per the batch rule but flagged in preset_rejected.
The prompt asks for a real WebGL scene, which is not a Roblox build target.

open_questions.ask: No setting was given - should the track read as city, desert, neon, or deliberately abstract?
The track is endless, so only a chunk can be framed - is a few-hundred-stud segment the right unit to draw?

coverage_missing.ask: What should the track and surroundings look like?
How many lanes - three, or something else?
Is distance the only score, or do coins count toward it too?

answers.ask: No setting was given - should the track read as city, desert, neon, or deliberately abstract?
answers.answer: Use a deliberately abstract, clean arcade runner look so the core movement and obstacles stay readable.

answers.ask: The track is endless, so only a chunk can be framed - is a few-hundred-stud segment the right unit to draw?
answers.answer: Yes, use a few-hundred-stud visible/recycled track segment; that is enough for this small endless runner.
